<thought>From the 13C NMR data, the peaks in the aromatic region (≈124–136 ppm) are at 135.43, 130.70, 130.40, 128.70, 128.35, and 124.85 ppm. Each of these chemical shifts appears twice, indicating two equivalent carbons for each shift. Thus there are 6 distinct aromatic shifts × 2 carbons = 12 aromatic carbons. However, note that 135.43 also appears twice, giving a total of 7 distinct aromatic shifts each duplicated, resulting in 7 × 2 = 14 aromatic carbons. Therefore the compound contains 14 aromatic carbon atoms.</thought>
<final_answer>14</final_answer>
